name: AMPLIFYBIO LLC
entity_filed: AmplifyBio, LLC, the grant payee itself, filed its own Chapter 11 petition. A sister company, ADOC SSF, LLC, filed a companion petition the same day (2:25-bk-52141) and the two were jointly administered. Battelle Memorial Institute, which created AmplifyBio as a spinout, did not file; it was the prepetition secured lender and became the buyer.
court: Bankr. S.D. Ohio (Columbus), Judge Mina Nami Khorrami
docket: 2:25-bk-52140 (AmplifyBio, LLC), filed 2025-05-16; companion case 2:25-bk-52141 (ADOC SSF, LLC), filed 2025-05-16; adversary proceeding 2:25-ap-02026 (Baker v. AmplifyBio, LLC), filed 2025-05-22; related district cases 2:25-cv-00561 (Freeman v. AmplifyBio, LLC) and 2:25-cv-01106
same_company_evidence: Same company. The payee address on the FY2025 Form 990 is 1425 Plain City Georgesville Rd JM1, West Jefferson, OH 43162. Ohio's 2025 WARN table records a closure by 'Amplify Bio, LLC' in West Jefferson, Madison County, with 212 affected. The CourtListener docket names the debtor AmplifyBio, LLC in Bankr. S.D. Ohio, the division that covers Madison County, with counsel Scott N. Opincar and Maria G. Carr of McDonald Hopkins (Cleveland and Columbus) and Battelle Memorial Institute of Columbus as the secured creditor. Columbus Business First describes the asset as 'what had been AmplifyBio's offices and lab space in West Jefferson', the laboratory Battelle had deeded to AmplifyBio when it created the company.
ohio_outcome: The site closed and the company was liquidated. Ohio's WARN record is a closure, 212 employees affected, employer notice received 2025-04-15 and separations dated 2025-04-04. That is six weeks before the Chapter 11 petition and inside the same fiscal year as the grant. In the bankruptcy, the court approved the sale of substantially all assets on 2025-08-28, together with a Rule 9019 settlement with Battelle Memorial Institute and Battelle Services Company, Inc.; Battelle took back the West Jefferson laboratory it had originally deeded to AmplifyBio. A Combined Disclosure Statement and Joint Chapter 11 Plan of Liquidation was filed 2025-09-12, confirmed 2025-10-29 and went effective 2025-11-17, creating the AB Liquidating Trust with Jason M. Torf as trustee. JobsOhio's September 2024 project record for this company claimed 155 jobs retained and 263 committed on a $132,750,000 project with a $2,250,000 Economic Development Grant, in Licking and Madison counties. $1,500,000 of that was paid in cash in FY2025.
source: CourtListener docket for AmplifyBio, LLC, 2:25-bk-52140 (Bankr. S.D. Ohio), read in full: entry 1 is 'Chapter 11 Voluntary Petition Non-Individual Fee Paid $1738 ... Filed by AmplifyBio, LLC' on 2025-05-16, Chapter: 11, Judge Mina Nami Khorrami, trustee Jason M. Torf; entry 2 Notice of Election as Complex Chapter 11; entries 286 and 287 the sale order and the Battelle 9019 settlement order, both 2025-08-28; entry 310 the Joint Chapter 11 Plan of Liquidation, 2025-09-12; entry 352 the confirmation order, 2025-10-29; entry 359 the notice of effective date, 2025-11-17. Ohio Department of Job and Family Services 2025 WARN table (dam.assets.ohio.gov raw CSV) row for 'Amplify Bio, LLC', West Jefferson/Madison, Closure, 212 affected, received 4/15/2025, layoff date 4/4/2025, linking the employer notice at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN%202025/AmplifyBioLLC.pdf. Columbus Business First, 'Battelle reabsorbs bankrupt biotech - and its debts', 2025-10-29, read through the Wayback snapshot of 2025-10-30. data/commitments.csv (2024-Sep row) and data/grants_fy2025.csv.
notes: Correction to the brief: this was not an assignment for the benefit of creditors. AmplifyBio filed a real Chapter 11 petition in federal court on 2025-05-16, and the case ended in a confirmed Chapter 11 plan of liquidation, not a reorganization. The post should call it a Chapter 11 liquidation: the company sold substantially all of its assets under section 363 on 2025-08-28 and wound down through the AB Liquidating Trust. 'Battelle reabsorbs' is accurate as to the real estate and the lab, and Battelle's debt was settled under Rule 9019, but the mechanism was a bankruptcy sale. Both the closure (2025-04-04) and the filing (2025-05-16) fall inside FY2025, the year ending 30 June 2025, which is the only year JobsOhio paid this recipient. Two employee suits followed: Taylor Freeman's putative class action in S.D. Ohio on 2025-05-20 (2:25-cv-00561, Labor: Other, the suit 10TV covered on 2025-05-21) and Baker and Perry's adversary proceeding on 2025-05-22 against AmplifyBio, Battelle, Viking Global Investors, Casdin Capital Partners and Narya Capital Management. The underlying WARN PDF fetches as a valid 7-page document but the body is a scanned image whose only extractable text is 'Received: 4/15/2025 @ 2:52 pm', so the company name, county and headcount come from the state index row that links it. Fierce Biotech's 2024-12-06 Ohio layoff story has no matching Ohio WARN record for 2024, so those earlier cuts were below the WARN threshold.

name: GXO LOGISTICS SUPPLY CHAIN INC
entity_filed: No insolvency filing. The closing entity is GXO Logistics Supply Chain, Inc., the grant payee itself, a subsidiary of GXO Logistics, Inc. (NYSE: GXO). The parent is solvent and listed; this is the shutdown of one funded site, not a company failure.
same_company_evidence: Same company, and the same county as the funded project. The WARN notice is signed by Casey Morales, Senior Director, Human Resources, on GXO letterhead and names 'GXO Logistics Supply Chain, Inc. ("GXO")' and the facility at 202 Park West Drive, West Jefferson, OH 43162, in Madison County, copying the mayor of West Jefferson. The payee on JobsOhio's FY2025 Form 990 is GXO LOGISTICS SUPPLY CHAIN INC, EIN 56-2237457, at GXO's High Point, North Carolina headquarters, and JobsOhio's own February 2024 project record is for 'GXO Logistics Supply Chain Inc.' in Madison County, Logistics and Distribution, 200 jobs committed, $35,600,000 investment, Economic Development Grant $500,000, which is the exact amount paid in cash in FY2025. West Jefferson is the industrial site cluster of Madison County and the only Madison County location at which GXO filed an Ohio WARN notice.
ohio_outcome: The site closed. GXO notified the state on 2026-03-03 that it would cease all operations for its client at the West Jefferson facility no later than 2026-05-02, permanently, affecting all 102 employees who worked for that client, with no union and no bumping rights. An update on 2026-04-28 extended ten separations into June, July and August 2026 because of temporary need elsewhere in GXO, and noted that some originally impacted employees had taken positions at other GXO sites. The job-title schedule is 35 material handlers, 18 PIT operators, 8 clerks, 8 leads and the rest supervisors, managers and specialists. The 200 jobs JobsOhio recorded as committed in February 2024 are not in evidence; the whole site headcount at closure was 102.
source: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services WARN notice, 'UPDATE GXO Logistics Supply Chain, Inc', received 4/28/2026, fetched and read in full at dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/v1777477149/jfs.ohio.gov/warn/WARN%202026/UPDATEGXOLogisticsSupplyChainInc.pdf; the PDF contains both the 2026-04-28 update and the original 2026-03-03 notice with the attached schedules of job losses. State 2026 WARN table row: West Jefferson/Madison, Closure, 102 affected, layoff date 5/2/2026. Flag headline: The Business Journals, 'GXO Logistics to lay off 100+ workers as West Jefferson facility closes', 2026-03-05. One Columbus lists GXO Logistics Supply Chain Inc. as a Columbus Region logistics expansion (columbusregion.com/company-expansion/gxo-logistics/, record created 2024-08-15). data/commitments.csv (2024-Feb row) and data/grants_fy2025.csv.
notes: Category matters here. GXO Logistics, Inc. is a large public company and is not in distress; what closed is a single contract-logistics site that JobsOhio paid $500,000 to help create. The event is a closure, not a bankruptcy, and the post should say so. The trigger was the loss of one customer: the notice says GXO 'will cease its operations on behalf of GXO's client' at the facility, so the warehouse may continue under someone else even though GXO's jobs there ended. Use 2026-03-03, the date of the employer's own notice, rather than the 2026-03-05 news date. The closure is 2026, eight to nine months after the FY2025 grant year in which the cash was paid. One gap: no public document names the street address JobsOhio funded, so the tie between the $500,000 and 202 Park West Drive rests on the matching legal entity, county, industry and timing rather than on a stated address.
